tb-E203-1.question:
What are the ‘lenses’ used in a transmission electron microscope made of?

A Glass

B Diamond

C Electromagnets

D Electrons
tb-E203-1.reasoning:
Moving electrons are charged and can be deflected by magnetic forces. In a TEM, electromagnets create fields that focus the electron beam, analogous to an optical convex lens focusing light.

These lenses are not glass or diamond optical lenses, nor are they made of electrons. Choose C.

tb-E203-2.question:
Which of the following properties does nano paint containing TiO2 nanoparticles have?

(1) Antibacterial

(2) Blocking ultra-violet radiation

(3) Self-cleaning

A (1) and (2) only

B (1) and (3) only

C (2) and (3) only

D (1), (2) and (3)
tb-E203-2.reasoning:
TiO₂ nanoparticles can absorb or scatter ultraviolet radiation. Under suitable illumination their photocatalytic activity can break down organic dirt and help suppress or destroy bacteria.

These mechanisms provide UV blocking, antibacterial and self-cleaning properties, with effectiveness depending on formulation and lighting. All three listed functions apply: D.

tb-E203-3.question:
Which of the following are the advantages of an STM over a TEM?

(1) An STM has a much higher resolving power.

(2) An STM can manipulate atoms.

(3) It is not necessary to make the sample very thin in using an STM.

A (1) and (2) only

B (1) and (3) only

C (2) and (3) only

D (1), (2) and (3)
tb-E203-3.reasoning:
An STM tip can manipulate surface atoms under suitable conditions. It measures tunnelling current at the surface, so electrons need not pass through the sample and an ultrathin specimen is unnecessary.

Both STM and TEM can achieve atomic-scale resolution; STM does not categorically have a much higher resolving power. Statements (2) and (3) are the listed advantages: C.

tb-E203-6.question:
Which of the following physical properties may change when a material is reduced to nano size?

(1) Melting point

(2) Transparency

(3) Electrical conductivity

A (1) and (2) only

B (1) and (3) only

C (2) and (3) only

D (1), (2) and (3)
tb-E203-6.reasoning:
At nanoscale sizes, a larger fraction of atoms lies at the surface, and size confinement can affect electronic states and motion. These effects can alter melting, light absorption or scattering, and charge transport.

Melting point, transparency and electrical conductivity may all change. The direction of each change depends on the material. All three are possible: D.

tb-E203-19.question:
Figure e shows a scanning tunnelling microscope (STM).

(a) Explain how an STM can attain atomic resolution. (3 marks)

(b) State a requirement for a sample to be imaged by an STM. (1 mark)

(c) A transmission electron microscope (TEM) can also attain atomic resolution. Suggest a situation in which

(i) an STM is preferred over a TEM,

(ii) a TEM is preferred over an STM in studying a sample. Assume the sample fulfils the requirement in (b). (2 marks)
tb-E203-19.answer:
(a) In an STM, the tip of its probe is formed by a single atom. 1A

A small potential difference is applied between the probe and the sample so that a tunnelling current flows between them. 1A

The size of the tunnelling current varies significantly when the tip-to-surface distance changes in atomic scale. 1A

Therefore, atomic resolution can be attained.

(b) It must conduct electricity. 1A

(Or other reasonable answers.)

(c) (i) The sample cannot be made very thin. 1A

(ii) The internal structure of the sample is being studied. 1A

(Or other reasonable answers.)
